record_note: Wired from the kit at the published revision 9f3ff726. The four kit fixes (tidy-baseline, gate-stage-guards, optimized-stage, git-index-file) are carried verbatim as probes in tools/kit-probes/ and their fixes are present in tools/ci.sh. adopted_fixes is intentionally EMPTY: adopted_in must name a commit in THIS repo, and nothing is committed yet (the orchestrator commits; the two-commit shape lands then). tools/kit-probes/consumer-subdirectory.sh is deliberately NOT listed here: it is a repo-local probe holding our own rule (a consumer gets JSONFuzz::core and nothing else), not a kit fix, and files[]/adopted_fixes are for artifacts that came FROM the kit. See the JSONFUZZ ADAPTATIONS item 6 in tools/ci.sh. **2026-10-06, record re-hash:** the checker reported this record BAD on repo_sha256 mismatch for 2 entries, edited after the record was written without this file being updated in the same commit — the one rule the convention says keeps it true. Re-hashed, no other field changed: tools/ci.sh (last edited d375d7a 2026-09-21 build: a consumer gets JSONFuzz::core and nothing else); INCIDENTS.md (last edited d375d7a 2026-09-21 build: a consumer gets JSONFuzz::core and nothing else). **2026-10-06, same card:** the checker also failed INCIDENTS.md on `adapted: false` with a file that is not byte-identical to the kit — it is the kit's log plus this repo's own entries, so the flag is corrected to `adapted: true` with the reason. No bytes were changed. **2026-10-06, hook-tier port:** adopted_fixes gains hook-tiers-agree and the revision moves to 919006e, that probe's copy point, with every kit_sha256 re-read there. tools/ci.sh and INCIDENTS.md are re-hashed. The tier variables and the hooks' `--fast`/`--full` dialect were already here; what this port fixed is that the header comment had drifted from the variables and that `format` was missing from the fast tier. **2026-10-06, card t_075c0a6f (KitCI fleet batch 2 of 3):** the gate is no longer a bash script. tools/ci.sh and the probes under tools/kit-probes/ are DELETED; the gate is the tracked gate.toml (13 stages, tiers fast/full) run by kit-ci, plus scripts/gate-env.sh, scripts/gate.sh and one scripts/<stage>.sh per stage — all of them this repo's own files, which is why none appears in files[] below. files[] loses tools/ci.sh and every tools/kit-probes/*.sh entry: the artifacts are gone, so no hash can describe them. The kit fixes those probes guarded move from adopted_fixes to declined_fixes — not because the fixes were declined, but because the artifact they CHECK no longer exists (each probe is written against a single bash gate file; measured against scripts/gate.sh, see INCIDENTS.md for the verdicts). The contracts did not go: each one has a named home, listed in INCIDENTS.md entry by entry. .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push are RE-HASHED because this commit edits them: they now NAME a tier (--tier fast, and --tier full with CI_REQUIRE_CLEAN=1, the old --require-clean flag moved into the environment), and their branch for this repo's own tools/ci.sh is gone with that file. `revision` and every other entry are UNCHANGED: nothing here came from the kit, and being behind the kit is not a failure. **2026-10-07, card t_c50bed30 (record repair after L3, finding 1 of 3):** the L3 promotion's checker run (card t_ae83c8e6) read RECORD BAD here -- 79 ok, 7 failed. Two `repo_sha256` values were stale: INCIDENTS.md and CLAUDE.md were edited after this record was written and their hashes did not follow them in the same commit, the one rule docs/KIT-REVISION-CONVENTION.md says keeps this record true. Re-hashed, no bytes changed: INCIDENTS.md `af03688401546a7d82c23b3e8cf975571363a79e9aeef7da6bc8797de5c40af4` -> `d4d9498ab18c6f2319428126591ec7628aeefcd27bd97a5e49dd852d012fb1dc`; CLAUDE.md `78a959a6e3eff7dc8e2eafce5758d4b69e1a5d56be4ec252f2cbce7fb41e9976` -> `4ae064500682cb4b6b16ae6f9e3123250eb6384afd3b2652ef722f92c91dc03e`. Five `declined_fixes` entries carried no `from_revision`: the 2026-10-06 conversion rewrote these lists mechanically, which dropped the field from the four entries it had moved out of adopted_fixes. Those four are kit fixes and take it from docs/KIT-FIXES.md's table: gate-stage-guards -> 951608c, git-index-file -> f9c3300, optimized-stage -> d531a11, tidy-baseline -> a6ad2ea (the two the sweep kept, format-checks-staged and hook-tiers-agree, already had theirs). The fifth, consumer-subdirectory, is NOT a kit fix, and the sweep should not have made an entry for it: the kit has never carried `probes/consumer-subdirectory.sh` (the named adds of `probes/*` in the kit's history are tidy-baseline, gate-stage-guards, optimized-stage, git-index-file, format-checks-staged, format-checks-staged-deno, hook-tiers-agree and gitignore-footprint -- it is none of them), and this repo's own INCIDENTS.md says so in as many words (2026-09-20 entry: 'This probe is NOT a kit fix: it is repo-local, and deliberately not listed in .ai-dev-starter.json's adopted_fixes (whose probe must name a path in the kit)'). It entered declined_fixes under a `why` that is false for it ('it guards the kit's templates/cpp/ci.sh' -- it guarded this repo's own CMake consumer rule), and the convention defines declined_fixes as the kit fixes this record does not carry, taken by a `probe` path that names a kit probe. There is no honest `from_revision` for a repo-local probe, so the entry is REMOVED rather than given one; the rule it held lives in scripts/consumer.sh and in that same INCIDENTS.md entry. `revision`, every `kit_sha256` and every other field are UNCHANGED.
